title: Speed complete Eisenstein replay by 35% with exact rational rank
body:
## Summary

Reduce complete Eisenstein replay wall time by 35.27% on the measured fixture, answering Open next question 2 of ywz65's #2627. This is a finite exact equivalence certificate and local performance measurement. The new contribution is an optional rational-rank adapter; the cost-40 theorem remains Jose Manuel's cited #2017 result.

```diff
  359 K-rank calls: retain ywz65's integer-pair adapter
  311 F4-rank calls: retain the original implementation
- 209 Q-rank calls: Fraction elimination
+ 209 Q-rank calls: denominator-cleared primitive integer rows
```

The adapter, verifier and benchmark were produced by Nick Petalas. Credit ywz65 #2627 for the K adapter and Q-rank handoff, Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml #2017 for the original verifier and theorem, and Jonathan Lam / Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled for geometry. Integer-row elimination is classical.

## Evidence

Six alternating fresh-process timing pairs after warmup, CPython 3.12.15 / macOS arm64:

- Before: median 0.436824 s, range 0.428594–0.498021 s.
- After: median 0.282744 s, range 0.278763–0.306366 s, 1.545x faster.
- Zero timed failures. Every run executes all 879 rank calls, retains all seven original rejection controls and compares complete stdout bytes.
- Separately, all 209 actual Q calls take median 0.198648 s before and 0.049803 s after. Q arithmetic is about 45% of the complete baseline. An untimed profile identified Fraction arithmetic as the main remaining cost.

`research/eisenstein-rational-rank/BENCHMARK.json` contains generated observations, order, environment, code hashes and the ordered matrix/rank digest. Shared-host load was uncontrolled; the nonoverlapping ranges support this local improvement, not a universal speed guarantee.

Local checks passed:

- Every actual Q-call comparison and input-preservation check; byte-identical complete replay.
- 1,798 rational matrices against a separate determinant/minor oracle, seven input/capacity controls and a wrong-adapter rejection through the original checks.
- Normal and optimized registered verification plus Git-free integrity, timed individually at 0.825 s, 0.845 s and 0.791 s. Each registered timeout is 60 s.
- All three live source corruptions reject before import.
- Metadata/pins, exact committed bytes/modes/source history, official export/input coverage, and normal/optimized read-only Git-free export replays.

From the repository root, standard-library Python 3.12 suffices:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -O -B research/eisenstein-rational-rank/replay.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -B research/eisenstein-rational-rank/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eisenstein-rational-rank
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/eisenstein-rational-rank --check-source-history --check-modes
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -O -B research/eisenstein-rational-rank/benchmark.py --output /absolute/new/path/benchmark.json
```

Any CPython 3.12 path can replace the displayed local interpreter. Timing output must be new and outside the checkout. Expected correctness markers are `PASS_EISENSTEIN_RATIONAL_RANK`, `PASS_EISENSTEIN_RATIONAL_INTEGRITY` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The rational adapter rejects inputs exceeding 96 rows/columns, 128-bit rational components or 4096-bit integer rows. Coefficient growth can change performance elsewhere. The fixture reaches 80 by 80 with four-bit input heights.

This adds no pairing theorem, native supplier, complete multiplication theorem, kappa improvement or selected-frontier change. No Lean, Docker, selected scientific cold replay, physical caller, compiler, stock or precision admission was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Frozen sources and production verifiers are untouched.

## Open next questions

Does this Q-rank adapter improve another named complete replay with larger ranks or coefficient heights? First capture that consumer's exact ordered matrix census and compare complete matched runs. Its coefficient bounds and actual workload are prerequisites; no further field optimization is included here.

## Related open work

The completion refresh examined the twelve other open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM: #5944, #5945, #5946, #5947, #5948, #5949, #5950, #5951, #5952, #5953, #5956 and #5957. None studies this Eisenstein Q-rank fixture or reports a competing timing for it. No additional computations were run to check those contributions. The rank-135 fitting matrix in #5950 and rational-frame cut certificate in #5944 concern different matrices and quantities.

#2627 and #2017 are merged predecessors. This contribution does not recount their mathematical results as new coverage. Unpublished work and arbitrary code diffs remain outside the overlap search.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed for `464b8c36e1de79422b2ad82b8a60a6732e4d50f6` in [run 40531800664](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40531800664): [plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40531800664/job/122286310633) in 4m40s and [replay (research/eisenstein-rational-rank)](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40531800664/job/122289096960) in 2m0s. The completed checks were read once, and the run head matches the PR head.

All three registered commands passed locally under CPython 3.12.15. Hosted replay certifies the bounded automated package checks, not independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance or a general performance guarantee. No CI failure remains.

## Merge danger

Door: reversible. Blast radius: one optional research package. No shared code, frozen input, production verifier or selected record changes.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19220187).
